## Why This Is Asked
This question tests choosing an architecture that stays Open-Closed, supports runtime extension of handlers, and keeps the ingestion core simple and testable.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Polymorphism
- Open-Closed Principle
- Registry-based dispatch

## Code Example
```javascript
interface FormatHandler { parse(input) }
class JsonHandler implements FormatHandler { parse(input) { /* parse JSON */ } }
class Ingestor { constructor(registry) { this.registry = registry } ingest(format, data) { return this.registry[format].parse(data) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle unknown formats at runtime?
- How would you test individual handlers and end-to-end ingestion?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a small, extensible plugin system using runtime registries and the separation of concerns between formatting and sinking.

## Key Concepts
- Registry pattern for dynamic extensibility
- Strategy/Factory for pluggable formatters
- Async I/O and backpressure in sinks
- Graceful shutdown and error containment

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Formatter { format(msg: string, level: string): string; }
interface Sink { write(data: string): Promise<void>; }
class Registry {
  private formats = new Map<string, Formatter>();
  private sinks = new Map<string, Sink>();
  registerFormat(name: string, f: Formatter): void
  getFormat(name: string): Formatter
  registerSink(name: string, s: Sink): void
  getSink(name: string): Sink
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test runtime registration of new formats?
- How would you prevent a slow sink from blocking others?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a pluggable, runtime-extendable auth system with strong tenant isolation, security, and observability. Demonstrates plugin loading, DI patterns, and security considerations critical at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Plugin architecture with dynamic loading
- Tenant isolation and per-tenant configuration
- Authentication flows: login, refresh, logout
- Security: short‑lived tokens, revocation, audit trails

## Code Example

```typescript
interface LoginRequest { provider: string; tenantId: string; credentials: any }
interface AuthResult { token: string; expiresAt: number }
interface AuthProvider {
  login(req: LoginRequest): Promise<AuthResult>
  refresh(token: string): Promise<AuthResult>
  logout(token: string): Promise<void>
}
interface ProviderFactory {
  create(tenantId: string, config: any): AuthProvider
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you version and hot-swap providers without downtime?
- How would you test provider isolation and revocation at scale?

## Why This Is Asked
Beginner-friendly exploration of extensibility and non-blocking I/O: add new sinks without changing core, and isolate failures per sink.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Plug-in pattern for runtime extension
- Registry mapping names to Sink implementations
- Non-blocking writes via per-sink queuing and worker pool
- Fault isolation and graceful degradation

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Sink { write(msg: string): Promise<void> }
class Registry { addSink(name: string, s: Sink): void; getSinks(): Sink[] }
class Logger { constructor(private reg: Registry) ; log(msg: string): void { for (const s of reg.getSinks()) s.write(msg); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test sink isolation and backpressure?
- How would you implement graceful shutdown for all sinks?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question assesses practical understanding of registry-driven pipelines and runtime extensibility, combining the Chain of Responsibility pattern with a pluggable transformer catalog. It tests the ability to evolve gateway behavior without modifying core routing logic.

## Key Concepts

- **Registry Pattern**: Dynamic component discovery by name at runtime
- **Chain of Responsibility / Pipeline**: Ordered execution of handlers
- **Stateless Transformers**: Pure functions that process and return requests
- **TypeScript Interfaces**: Type-safe contract for pluggable components
